gates.note: Vendor identity (Taiwan Economic Journal Co., Ltd. / 台灣經濟新報文化事業股份有限公司, tejwin.com) is confirmed for all 8 datasets. Official product name was additionally confirmed via a citable, publicly-reachable TEJ page for 7/8 datasets (all but revenue_growth). Per §10.2, Gate R4-A requires vendor identity AND official product name AND licensing/access terms, all documented from the provider's own materials. Every page Phase B attempted this round was, in fact, reachable (access_status ACCESSIBLE throughout, see provenance_citations.csv) -- no login/payment/download wall was ever actually encountered. The FAIL is not because access was blocked; it is because the licensing/access-terms content simply does not appear anywhere on the pages that were reached, and (for revenue_growth only) the official product name does not either. Gate R4-A therefore FAILs for every dataset -- a valid, complete, terminal finding (AC-R4-31), not a defect requiring further searching, and not overstated as a login-blocked result it was not.

phase_b_execution_compliance_statement: This Phase B pass is NOT reported as a fully compliant Phase B completion. Gate R4-A/R4-L/R4-X's diagnostic findings (FAIL/FAIL/FAIL, per gate_results.json above) may still be read on their own evidentiary merits -- they are independent of, and are not invalidated by, this execution-compliance finding. But the two are separate questions: gate findings answer 'what does the evidence show about the datasets/live identity/derived-output reliance'; phase_b_execution_compliance answers 'did this Phase B pass itself stay within the read-only, zero-byte-copy boundary the approved prereg requires (§5/§8/§11/§11.1/AC-R4-35)' -- and the answer to the second question is no, because of the disclosed PDF-fetch side effect. Whether to accept this deviation, archive it as-is, require remediation, or take any other action is a decision reserved to the human reviewer -- this report does not decide it, recommend a specific resolution, or presume the deviation is acceptable merely because it was unintentional and unused.
